fix: derive window_started_at from transcript timestamps, not stale counter

Session windows now derive their start time from the earliest actual transcript
message, not from the counter file's potentially-stale value. This prevents
artificial bloat when commits are sparse and days pass without work — the window
always reflects reality (when work started) rather than stale state.

Backfixed the June 19 entry that incorrectly spanned 11 days (265 hours) due to
the counter not being reset for 11 days; now correctly shows 0.5 hours (from
11:41 AM when work started to 12:08 PM when it was committed).

Revert "test: verify post-commit enrichment after skill reset"

This reverts commit 1efe2ef3f7c87f7a1be3fa8ea07657ff181d36ea.

fix: use 30-minute fallback window to avoid capturing stale cached context

Token counts were inflated 4-5x because window_started_at spanned from hours
earlier, retroactively including all cached context from that entire period.
Now use 30-minute fallback so we capture only recent interaction without
stale cached prompts from long ago.

fix: stop attributing cache_read_tokens to current sessions

Cache reads represent previously-cached prompts from earlier sessions, not
work done in the current session. Including them inflates token counts 5-10x
and misattributes cache efficiency gains to the wrong session.

Now we log only: input + output + cache_writes (actual work done today).
Cache reads are skipped to match how the extension attributes them.

fix: dual-write telemetry directly to Neon instead of local Docker

Both the post-commit hook and end-session skill now write to Neon prod DB
via psql + NEON_DATABASE_URL from backend/.env. This replaces the docker

Every commit and session now lands in prod immediately, automatically.
fix: read NEON_DATABASE_URL from root .env not backend/.env

fix: cap session window at 4h to prevent multi-day gap inflation

The git-based window derivation (prev commit → current commit) has an
edge case: when commits span a multi-day pause, the previous commit
timestamp is too stale to be a valid session boundary. A 7-day gap
between the June 22nd commit and the first June 29th commit produced
a 167h session that swept the entire transcript history, inflating
the dashboard to ~178h when the true total was ~11h.

Fix: add a MAX_SESSION_HOURS=4 cap in the post-commit hook. If the
previous commit is more than 4h before the current one, clamp the
window to 30 minutes before the current commit instead.

Also: delete the bad 167h row (id f1cf1dfb) from both ai_sessions.jsonl
and Neon. Dashboard now shows ~11h which matches expected total.

Audit page updated with Fix 4 and revised data trust levels.

feat: GitHub Actions CI/CD + commit_pushed event + deploy history dashboard

STEP 1 — .github/workflows/deploy.yml
Two-job pipeline: ci (pytest + npm build) gates deploy (Render hook + Vercel
CLI --prod). After both deploys are triggered, emits a commit_pushed event to
POST /api/events/internal with commit sha, branch, actor, and workflow run id.
Event emission is best-effort (continue-on-error) since Render free tier may
be sleeping immediately after a cold-start deploy.

STEP 2 — POST /api/events/internal
New auth-gated endpoint in backend/app/events/router.py. Protected by
X-Internal-Secret header matching INTERNAL_API_SECRET env var (set in Render
environment + GitHub Actions secrets). Returns 403 for any missing/wrong secret.
Writes directly to the events table via psycopg.

STEP 3 — Deploy history on dashboard
GET /api/telemetry/deploys returns total/7d/24h counts + last 10 commit_pushed
events. Dashboard page fetches this server-side and renders a "Deploy history"
section above System Status: frequency cards + commit list with sha, message,
actor, branch, and timestamp. Shows a placeholder when no deploys are recorded yet.

Note: disable auto-deploy on Vercel and Render to avoid double deploys once
GitHub Actions secrets are configured. See DECISIONS.md for full rationale.

Cache-read tokens were correctly excluded from total_tokens (the 'work
effort' metric) to avoid 5-10x inflation. But the cost formula also
